K-Means playground

1st ROW : K-means on the portrait's pixel COLORS (BGR - works for any channel set); each pixel is replaced by its cluster's center, quantizing the image into the chosen number of colors
2nd ROW : Group the inpaint_mask_holes.png mask components by their positions and sizes (centroid + area)
3rd ROW : Cluster the Shi-Tomasi corner points of the 'K N T' canvas by their positions
4th ROW : Cluster the drawn letters/symbols by SHAPE alone (no position): holes, extent, loose ends, convexity defects, corner count

CV K-Means Colors

cv2.kmeans with KMEANS_PP_CENTERS over the float32 pixel stack (CV_32F is asserted). 

Input may be IMAGE, MASK or NPARRAY; for an IMAGE the quantized output has the same 8-bit range.
The palette strip is 64 x (64*K) swatches sorted by coverage (most common color first).

CV K-Means Mask Clusters

Groups the regions of a mask into `clusters` groups and returns one mask per group (largest first) plus their bounding boxes. A single mask is split into its connected blobs; a MASK batch is one region per frame. 'properties' picks any set of columns (position, area, aspect ratio, circularity, orientation, mean colour...), so 'no position | area' clusters by SIZE alone. The columns are z-scored, so each one counts equally; switch 'scale' to raw/image-relative to weigh a raw area against a raw centroid instead.

The 'properties' checkboxes live on the Region Properties node INSIDE this subgraph. A promoted subgraph input is a bare SOCKET - no widget comes with it - so to pick the columns from the outside, drop a 'CV Region Property Flags' node on the canvas (the same checkboxes, one STRING output) and wire it into 'properties'. Unconnected, the value on the inner node applies.

widgets_values:
CV K-Means Points

Clusters a point set into k groups (cv2.kmeans), the point-array sibling of the 'CV K-Means Colors' and 'CV K-Means Mask Clusters' blueprints.

Zero points are valid: 'success' is false, 'labels' and 'centers' come back empty and nothing raises. cv2.kmeans itself asserts on an empty sample set, so the data path swaps in a one-point dummy and the result path throws it away.
